headline: University of Copenhagen will merge its theology faculty into humanities after 549 years
deck: Law and social sciences will merge too in 2028; two other faculties split in 2029, leaving six.
standard: The University of Copenhagen will merge its Faculty of Theology, one of the four faculties it was founded with in 1479, into a joint Faculty of Humanities and Theology on 1 January 2028. Law and social sciences will merge on the same day. In 2029 the health and science faculties will each split in two, which leaves the university with six faculties.

The university says most students will notice nothing, because programmes will not change. David Dreyer Lassen, the rector, says in a statement that the faculties have grown very unequal in size and complexity, which strains the university's leadership.
Martin Ravn, a theologian and parish priest, told Kristeligt Dagblad the restructuring made him 'worried about theology's future as a university subject'.
short: The University of Copenhagen will merge its Faculty of Theology, one of its four original faculties from 1479, into a joint Faculty of Humanities and Theology on 1 January 2028. The university says programmes will not change.
